A1.justification: Both PDFs describe History-Guided Video Diffusion. Their complete main text, Appendices A–D, supplementary visuals, tables, and equations support reliable comparison despite pagination changes.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix D report original video-generation experiments and robot imitation-learning results, including FVD, LPIPS, VBench scores, and task success rates.

after.justification: The later version retains the original video-generation and robot experiments, including quantitative benchmarks and supplementary qualitative results.

M1.justification: The DFoT architecture, per-frame noise training objective, history-guidance variants, Algorithm 1, and extended temporal guidance in Appendix A.8 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use Kinetics-600, RealEstate10K, Minecraft, and Fruit Swapping, retaining the same interpolation, long-video, OOD-history, and robot-perturbation scenarios.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain SD, FS, BD, the same literature baselines in Table 1, and the same robot-policy comparators. Updated citation years do not identify new comparison methods.

E3.justification: Appendix C retains the evaluation metrics, model configurations, budgets, and protocols, including the 50K-video Kinetics benchmark, 64-frame rollout evaluation, and camera-rotation binning.

E4.justification: The guidance-scale sweeps, binary-dropout ablation, fine-tuning and EMA analyses, OOD-history tests, and stronger robot-perturbation cases are retained without additional or revised analyses.

E5.justification: Appendix C.4 retains three random seeds for the Kinetics benchmark, and Table 1 retains its uncertainty reporting. No repeated-run or statistical estimation practice changes.

E6.justification: Numerical and qualitative results are unchanged. Table 1 retains DFoT FVD values of 4.3±0.1 and 4.7±0.0; Appendix D retains the 170.4 rollout FVD and robot success rates of 83% and 28% under their respective perturbation settings.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1, Definition A.2 corrects the learned-model factorization from forward conditionals to reverse denoising conditionals, conditioning the cleaner state on the noisier state. This aligns the definition with the existing proof; theorem statements and remaining derivations are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about flexible history conditioning, guidance benefits, efficient fine-tuning, and stable long-video generation.

C2.justification: Interpretations of guidance tradeoffs, OOD generalization, scaling limitations, and robot failure conditions are unchanged. The added Impact Statement contains only general misuse caveats.

D1.justification: Table 2 and Appendix C retain the same implementation, hyperparameter, hardware, and training details. The explicit project URL in v2 points to the same destination already linked by v1's 'this URL'; resource access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: Reference changes update publication metadata and consolidate duplicate DDPM entries. Matching works across these updates establishes unchanged cited-work coverage and research positioning in Section 2 and Appendix B.

P1.justification: V2 corrects the Section 4 heading, updates affiliations and publication information, displays the project URL explicitly, and adds acknowledgements and an Impact Statement. Reference metadata is refreshed, while the scientific narrative and section organization remain stable.

P2.justification: V2 introduces limited page and column reflow and adds running title headers to Appendices B–D. The same 17 figures and two tables retain their visual content, captions, and organization.

improvement.justification: Correcting the conditional direction in Definition A.2 resolves a local inconsistency with the reverse-process factorization used in the ELBO proof. Editorial and bibliographic cleanup adds modest polish. These are limited improvements; the methods, empirical evidence, and conclusions remain unchanged.
